drills.hint: upper bound of the default NodePort range (a number)
drills.note: The default range is 30000-32767. The API server flag --service-node-port-range can change it.
drills.prompt: By default, NodePort Services get a port in the range 30000-___.
With the default cluster domain, Service 'api' in namespace 'shop' resolves at api.shop.svc.___

drills.note: 'port' is the port the Service exposes. 'targetPort' is the port on the pod it forwards to.
drills.prompt: Which field in a Service port entry sets the port the container actually listens on?

drills.note: ExternalName only works at the DNS level. No proxying or virtual IP is involved.
drills.prompt: Which Service type has no selector and makes DNS return a CNAME to an external hostname?

answers: The pod's resolv.conf has search domains such as shop.svc.cluster.local, so the short name 'api' is expanded to api.shop.svc.cluster.local.
drills.note: With the default dnsPolicy ClusterFirst, the kubelet adds namespace-based search domains to every pod's resolv.conf.
drills.prompt: Explain why a pod in namespace 'shop' can reach Service 'api' using just the name 'api'.

focus_note: Pods come and go and their IPs change, so clients talk to a Service instead. The Service's selector matches pod labels, and kube-proxy (or a replacement in the CNI plugin) forwards traffic from the Service's virtual IP to the matching pods. Cluster DNS adds a name for each Service. For example, Service 'api' in namespace 'shop' resolves at api.shop.svc.cluster.local.
subtitle: Stable addresses for changing pods
title: Services and Cluster DNS

vocab.example: The backend Service is a ClusterIP, so only pods in the cluster can call it.
vocab.example_translation: The Service gets an internal virtual IP and is not exposed outside the cluster.
meanings: virtual IP reachable only inside the cluster

vocab.example: The StatefulSet uses a headless Service so each database pod gets its own DNS record.
vocab.example_translation: No virtual IP is allocated. DNS returns the individual pod addresses instead.
meanings: Service whose DNS returns pod IPs directly
